```{r setup}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(fig.width = 7.2, fig.height = 4.0, dpi = 300, dev = "png")
library(dplyr)
library(knitr)
library(ggplot2)

repo_root <- if (file.exists("Second Step/results/results_all.csv")) {
  "."
} else if (file.exists("../Second Step/results/results_all.csv")) {
  ".."
} else {
  stop("Cannot locate Second Step/results/results_all.csv")
}

results <- read.csv(
  file.path(repo_root, "Second Step/results/results_all.csv"),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)
conditions <- read.delim(
  file.path(repo_root, "conditions.tsv"),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE,
  na.strings = ""
)

results <- results |>
  mutate(
    arm = sub("_[0-9]+$", "", agent_id),
    arm = factor(arm, levels = conditions$condition),
    years_start = as.integer(years_start),
    years_end = as.integer(years_end),
    year_span = years_end - years_start + 1,
    cov_none = grepl("^none$|^$", tolower(trimws(covariates))),
    est_lc = tolower(trimws(estimator)),
    twfe = grepl("twfe|feols|fixest", est_lc),
    continuous_tx = grepl("continuous", tolower(treatment_definition))
  )

arm_summary <- results |>
  group_by(arm) |>
  summarize(
    n = n(),
    mean_att = mean(att_estimate, na.rm = TRUE),
    sd_att = sd(att_estimate, na.rm = TRUE),
    median_att = median(att_estimate, na.rm = TRUE),
    frac_negative = mean(att_estimate < 0, na.rm = TRUE),
    frac_teen = mean(outcome_variable == "emp_pop_ratio_teen", na.rm = TRUE),
    frac_no_cov = mean(cov_none, na.rm = TRUE),
    frac_twfe = mean(twfe, na.rm = TRUE),
    frac_continuous = mean(continuous_tx, na.rm = TRUE),
    mean_start = mean(years_start, na.rm = TRUE),
    mean_span = mean(year_span, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

between_arm_ss <- function(values, arms) {
  arms <- droplevels(as.factor(arms))
  overall_mean <- mean(values, na.rm = TRUE)
  arm_means <- tapply(values, arms, mean, na.rm = TRUE)
  arm_counts <- table(arms)
  sum(arm_counts[names(arm_means)] * (arm_means - overall_mean)^2)
}

set.seed(42)
obs_stat <- between_arm_ss(results$att_estimate, results$arm)
perm_stats <- replicate(10000, {
  between_arm_ss(results$att_estimate, sample(results$arm))
})
fisher_p <- mean(perm_stats >= obs_stat)
kw <- kruskal.test(att_estimate ~ arm, data = results)

fmt <- function(x, d = 4) sprintf(paste0("%.", d, "f"), x)
```

\newpage

## Executive summary

This project tests whether **prompted literature priors** causally change what autonomous AI agents report about the employment effects of the minimum wage. Agents analyze the **same** state–year panel with the **same** task instructions; only the literature context (if any) is randomized.

**Design.** Five arms × 50 Cursor agents = **250** completed analyses. Arms: no prime; null-effect short; null-effect with citations; negative-effect short; negative-effect with citations. Agents choose outcome, sample window, treatment definition, covariates, and estimator under a shared DiD methodology guide.

**Headline results (Second Step run).**

| Finding | Result |
|:--------|:-------|
| Completion | **250/250** agents returned usable `results.csv` |
| Between-arm ATT differences | **Not significant** (Fisher omnibus *p* = `r fmt(fisher_p)`; Kruskal–Wallis *p* = `r fmt(kw$p.value)`) |
| Outcome choice | **~99.6%** studied teen employment-to-population |
| Estimator choice | **~98.8%** Callaway–Sant'Anna family; **≤4% TWFE** in any arm |
| Treatment definition | **249/250 binary**; **0% continuous** MW treatment |
| Short vs citation-rich primes | **No meaningful ATT gap** on planned contrasts |

**Bottom line.** With Cursor `composer-2` agents and Wave-2-style estimator discretion (TWFE allowed), **literature primes did not shift reported ATTs** in a detectable way. Behavior resembles Cunningham's **constrained Wave 1** (CS-heavy, overlapping distributions) more than his **Wave 2** finding that negatively primed Claude Code agents moved toward TWFE, continuous treatment, and more negative estimates.

**Implication.** Primed priors alone are not enough: **platform, model, and instruction packaging** appear to mediate whether discretion produces estimator-channel divergence.

---

## 1. Purpose and motivation

Many-analyst studies show that researchers facing identical data can report different causal estimates through **specification choices**. Borjas & Breznau (2026, *Science Advances*) linked immigration researchers' priors to their estimates. Scott Cunningham's design turns that association into an **experiment** by randomizing the prior via a literature prime while holding data and task fixed ([Substack write-up](https://causalinf.substack.com/p/claude-code-45-ai-agents-and-the)).

This repository is a **Cursor SDK replication / extension** of Cunningham's `mw-analyst-experiment` design (originally Claude Code CLI).

**Research question:** Do literature primes about minimum-wage employment effects causally shift autonomous agents' reported average treatment effects (ATTs)?

---

## 2. Experimental design

### Arms

| Arm ID | Label | Literature file |
|:-------|:------|:----------------|
| `none` | None | *(none)* |
| `null_short` | Null Short | `PRIME_NULL_SHORT.md` |
| `null_cites` | Null Cites | `PRIME_NULL_CITES.md` |
| `negative_short` | Negative Short | `PRIME_NEGATIVE_SHORT.md` |
| `negative_cites` | Negative Cites | `PRIME_NEGATIVE_CITES.md` |

All agents receive: `agent_panel_essential.csv`, `DATA_DICTIONARY.md`, `DID_METHODOLOGY.md`, and `INSTRUCTIONS_SHARED.md`. Primed arms also receive one literature context file.

### What agents decide

- Employment outcome (CPS subgroups, QCEW industries, etc.)
- Treatment definition (binary staggered vs continuous)
- Sample years / states
- Covariates and comparison group
- Estimator (Callaway–Sant'Anna, continuous DiD, TWFE, etc.)

### Deliverables per agent

1. **`results.csv`** — one row with design choices and ATT / SE / CI  
2. **`llms.txt`** — structured narrative of the analysis  

### Data

Pre-aggregated **state × year** panel (51 units, 1990–2022): effective minimum wages, CPS employment rates for multiple groups, and selected QCEW industry series.

### Scale and waves

| Wave | Location | Scale | Notes |
|:-----|:---------|:------|:------|
| First | Frozen in `First Step/` | 150 agents (30×5) | Earlier protocol; TWFE discouraged |
| Second (current results) | `Second Step/results/` | **250 agents (50×5)** | TWFE allowed in methodology |

---

## 3. Technical pipeline

| Component | Role |
|:----------|:-----|
| `@cursor/sdk` + `launch_experiment_cursor.mjs` | Local agents in isolated temp workspaces |
| `run_full_experiment.sh` / `run_pilot_one_per_condition.sh` | Full (250) and pilot (5) launchers |
| `collect_results.sh` | Aggregate outputs → `Second Step/results/` |
| `analyze_results.R` | Omnibus tests, plots |
| `analyze_second_step_detail.R` | Extended tables/figures → `Second Step/analysis/` |

Default model: **`composer-2`**. Agents are sandboxed with `settingSources: []` so user/project rules outside the workspace are not loaded.

---

## 4. Key results

### Arm-level ATT summary

```{r arm-table}
arm_summary |>
  transmute(
    Arm = as.character(arm),
    N = n,
    `Mean ATT` = fmt(mean_att),
    `SD` = fmt(sd_att),
    `Median` = fmt(median_att),
    `% neg.` = fmt(100 * frac_negative, 1),
    `% teen` = fmt(100 * frac_teen, 1),
    `% TWFE` = fmt(100 * frac_twfe, 1),
    `Mean span` = fmt(mean_span, 1)
  ) |>
  kable(booktabs = TRUE, align = c("l", rep("r", 8)))
```

### Inference

- **Fisher omnibus** (between-arm sum of squares, 10,000 permutations): observed = `r fmt(obs_stat)`, *p* = `r fmt(fisher_p)`.
- **Kruskal–Wallis** across five arms: χ² = `r fmt(kw$statistic)`, *p* = `r fmt(kw$p.value)`.
- Planned contrasts (null − negative, short and cites): neither rejects at conventional levels.

**Interpretation:** condition labels are statistically exchangeable with respect to reported ATT in this run.

```{r fig-att, fig.cap="Distribution of reported ATT estimates by treatment arm (N = 250)."}
knitr::include_graphics(file.path(repo_root, "Second Step/results/att_by_arm.png"))
```

```{r fig-forest, fig.cap="Arm-level mean ATT with approximate 95% intervals."}
knitr::include_graphics(file.path(repo_root, "Second Step/analysis/forest_arm_means.png"))
```

### Specification patterns

- **Outcome:** nearly universal teen EMP/POP (`emp_pop_ratio_teen`).
- **Estimator:** Callaway–Sant'Anna dominates; TWFE rare and not concentrated in negative arms.
- **Treatment:** almost entirely binary staggered MW changes.
- **Covariates:** nontrivial share use none (~42–66% by arm); not clearly sorted by prime.
- **Event studies:** produced by ≥98% of agents per arm.

```{r fig-estimator, fig.cap="Estimator family composition by arm."}
knitr::include_graphics(file.path(repo_root, "Second Step/analysis/estimator_family_stacked_by_arm.png"))
```

## 5. Comparison to Cunningham (2026)

| Dimension | Cunningham (Substack) | This Cursor run |
|:----------|:----------------------|:----------------|
| Platform | Claude Code CLI | Cursor SDK (`composer-2`) |
| Arms | 3 | **5** (short vs cites splits + pure none) |
| Wave 1 pattern | Similar ATTs under CS-only | **Replicates in spirit** (~99% CS; Fisher *p* ≈ 0.41) |
| Wave 2 pattern | Negative arm → more TWFE, continuous Tx, more negative ATTs | **Does not replicate** (≤4% TWFE; 0% continuous) |
| Data | Same essential panel concept | Pre-aggregated CSV (no microdata rebuild) |

Most plausible explanation for the missing Wave 2 shift: **model/platform defaults** toward Callaway–Sant'Anna despite TWFE permission, possibly interacting with prime packaging and stricter Cursor sandboxing. A fuller technical discussion is in `reports/cursor_replication_report.qmd`.

## 7. Limitations and next steps

**Limitations.** Single model (`composer-2`); no rhetoric/confidence scoring pipeline; one permissive-estimator wave on Cursor (no within-platform CS-only vs TWFE-allowed contrast); prime texts differ from Cunningham's exact wording.

**Testable next steps.**

1. Match Cunningham's three-arm primes and Wave 2 methodology text verbatim.  
2. Re-run with a Claude model via Cursor SDK (if available), holding instructions fixed.  
3. Inspect agent logs for abandoned TWFE trials (mechanism check).  
4. Optionally relax sandbox (`settingSources`) to test ambient-memory hypotheses.
